hunks.baseline: As I charged, the spearhead shot forward like a flash of light, cleaving through space. Flames surged up, burning the air and erasing the wind as they pierced the thick darkness.
hunks.sol: As I charged, the spearhead flashed forward, cleaving through space. Flames surged up, burning the air and erasing the wind as they pierced the thick darkness.

hunks.baseline: A single point, piercing the invisible flow with perfect precision.
hunks.sol: One precise point pierced the invisible flow.

hunks.baseline: Some of the magical power sweeping toward me like a wave dispersed helplessly. My vision plunged through the gap in the magical power at the same speed as my thrust—and a familiar face came into view.
hunks.sol: Some of the magical power sweeping toward me like a wave scattered. I drove through the gap at full speed, and a familiar face came into view.

hunks.baseline: No, perhaps it was more accurate to call it a face that was both familiar and strange.
hunks.sol: No. Familiar and strange at once.

hunks.baseline: Because the Michael Silbert standing there now was no longer Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: Because the Michael Silbert standing there was no longer Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: “You’re not bad.”
hunks.sol: “Not bad.”

hunks.baseline: Instead of panicking when my target disappeared from sight in an instant, I twisted around in a movement closer to instinct.
hunks.sol: My target disappeared from sight, but instead of panicking, I twisted around on instinct.

hunks.baseline: A sword suddenly rose behind me, skimming my side and cutting through empty air.
hunks.sol: A sword sprang up behind me, skimmed my side, and stabbed through empty air.

hunks.baseline: If I hadn’t dodged, that strike would have pierced my heart. I spun around and thrust out a palm.
hunks.sol: If I hadn’t dodged, it would have pierced my heart. I spun and struck with my palm.

hunks.baseline: He was supposed to have a body made of flesh and bone. Yet the instant our palms collided, a blast like an explosion rang out.
hunks.sol: His body was supposed to be flesh and bone. Yet when our palms met, the impact sounded like an explosion.

hunks.baseline: Along with a shock wave greater than an explosion—
hunks.sol: And the shock wave hit even harder.

hunks.baseline: The ground flipped over beneath my sliding toes. Unlike Michael Silbert, who stood rooted to the spot, I was pushed back several meters. He curled up the corner of his mouth.
hunks.sol: The ground tore up beneath my sliding feet. I was driven back several meters while Michael Silbert stood rooted to the spot. One corner of his mouth curled upward.

hunks.baseline: Instead of answering, I spat the blood pooled in my mouth onto the ground. Before it even hit the earth, I stepped forward with all my strength.
hunks.sol: I spat out the blood pooled in my mouth instead of answering. Before it hit the ground, I stepped forward with all my strength.

hunks.baseline: The ground beneath my toes shattered like an explosion.
hunks.sol: The ground shattered beneath my foot.

hunks.baseline: The wind swept past my body, and the distance of more than ten meters disappeared in an instant. My spear and his sword flashed toward each other.
hunks.sol: Wind swept over me as I crossed more than ten meters in an instant. My spear and his sword flashed toward each other.

hunks.baseline: The sharp clash burst the air around us. The sword had grown so long and massive that it could hardly be called a sword anymore, as if to prove the magical power overflowing from it. It drove my spearhead far aside.
hunks.sol: The sharp clash burst the air around us. His sword had grown so long and massive it hardly looked like a sword anymore, swollen with magical power. It knocked my spearhead far aside.

hunks.baseline: This wasn’t just a difference in physical ability. It came down to the sheer amount of power we held.
hunks.sol: This wasn’t just a difference in physical ability. It was a difference in the sheer amount of power we held.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert’s body had undoubtedly grown much stronger after absorbing the Magic Gem. And with the magical power welling up without end, he could reinforce it even further. Of course I was being pushed back.
hunks.sol: Absorbing the Magic Gem had made Michael Silbert’s body much stronger, and the magical power welling up without end reinforced it further. Of course he was pushing me back.

hunks.baseline: At least, as long as I insisted on a head-on fight.
hunks.sol: As long as I insisted on fighting him head-on.

hunks.baseline: Suddenly, I smoothly rotated the spearhead, and the sword blade slid along it.
hunks.sol: I turned my spearhead in a smooth arc, and his blade slid along it.

hunks.baseline: Despite the enormous difference in force, Michael Silbert’s sword slipped free of its owner’s control. Certain that my hunch had been right, I thrust a fist at him.
hunks.sol: Despite the enormous difference in force, Michael Silbert’s sword slipped out of his control. My hunch confirmed, I drove a fist toward him.

hunks.baseline: The thick darkness moved like a living creature and hurried to envelop its master, but my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, thrown with all my strength, burned through the magical power and slammed into his chest.
hunks.sol: The thick darkness moved like a living creature, rushing to envelop its master. But my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist burned through the magical power and slammed into his chest.

hunks.sol: A deafening crash rang out, and his body flew away like a cannonball.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert hurriedly flung out both arms, pouring magical power at me to keep me in check. Then he coughed up blood.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert hastily flung out both arms, pouring magical power toward me to keep me back. Then he coughed up blood.

hunks.baseline: I cut down every bolt of magical power flying toward me and watched him stagger. A strange feeling stirred in me.
hunks.sol: I cut down every bolt flying toward me and watched him stagger. Something strange stirred in me.

hunks.baseline: “So even a monster like you is still human—for now, anyway.”
hunks.sol: “So even a monster like you is still human. For now, anyway.”

hunks.baseline: At my mutter, Michael Silbert clenched his teeth.

hunks.baseline: But his eyes wavered. He hadn’t expected that blow.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at my mutter. His eyes trembled; he hadn’t expected that blow.

hunks.baseline: “What the hell did you do?”
hunks.sol: “What did you do?”

hunks.baseline: “You don’t need to understand. There’s a shitload of things in this world you don’t know about anyway.”
hunks.sol: “You don’t need to understand. There’s a shitload of things in this world you don’t know about.”

hunks.baseline: “So I don’t bother trying to understand, either. You, or those lunatics fighting over there—who knows what kind of fucked-up shit they got up to while working with you to end up in that fight? None of it makes any sense to me.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t bother trying to understand, either. You, or those lunatics fighting over there. Who knows what kind of fucked-up shit they’ve done with you to end up in that fight? None of it makes sense to me.”

hunks.baseline: I stared straight at Michael Silbert and continued.
hunks.sol: I stared straight at Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: “No. The moment I understood it, I’d become the same kind of idiot.”
hunks.sol: “No. The moment it did, I’d be the same kind of idiot.”

hunks.baseline: A new emotion covered the traces of pain on his face.
hunks.sol: A new emotion spread across his face, over the traces of pain.

hunks.baseline: Watching his face twist was far more satisfying than I’d expected.
hunks.sol: Watching his face twist felt better than I’d expected.

hunks.baseline: “I told you earlier. A leech is still just a leech. Even if it died and came back to life, it could never become a dragon.”
hunks.sol: “I told you earlier. A leech is still a leech. It couldn’t become a dragon even if it died and came back to life.”

hunks.baseline: “……You bastard.”
hunks.sol: “You bastard…”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. Whatever else, I’ll admit one thing.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. Putting everything else aside, I’ll give you one thing.”

hunks.baseline: My breath was hot with heat, like that of a fire dragon. I stepped toward him and added,
hunks.sol: My breath was as hot as a fire dragon’s. I stepped toward him.

hunks.baseline: With that, I launched White Flame, gripped in reverse, without hesitation.
hunks.sol: With that, I hurled White Flame without hesitation, gripping it in reverse.

hunks.baseline: The air burst in layers, as if a sonic boom had just gone off.
hunks.sol: The air burst in layer after layer, as if a sonic boom had gone off.

hunks.baseline: And at the end of it stood Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: And at the end of its path stood Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: An enormous explosion of flame and magical power.
hunks.sol: Flame and magical power erupted together.

hunks.baseline: The stained glass, which had barely held its shape thanks to dozens of layers of defensive magic, couldn’t withstand the shock wave and shattered. I flashed through the rain of countless shards falling overhead and thrust out both palms.
hunks.sol: Dozens of layers of defensive magic had barely kept the stained glass intact. The shock wave finally shattered it, and I flashed through the rain of shards pouring down overhead, striking with both palms.

hunks.baseline: A gale filled with flame swept through.
hunks.sol: A gale of flame swept through the room.

hunks.baseline: Amid the surroundings blurred by the explosion, the shadow of someone staggering was etched clearly into my eyes.
hunks.sol: Amid the haze left by the explosion, I caught a clear glimpse of someone staggering.

hunks.baseline: There was no room for doubt.
hunks.sol: No doubt about it.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I kicked off the ground and charged, reaching out to grab empty air.
hunks.sol: I kicked off the ground and charged, reaching out to grab empty air.

hunks.baseline: No—two spears appeared as if drawn into existence by the command I shouted in my mind. I caught them and launched them once more.
hunks.sol: No—at the command I shouted in my mind, two spears appeared as though drawn into existence. I caught them and hurled them after the first.

hunks.baseline: Two streaks of light tore across the space between us.
hunks.sol: Two streaks of light crossed the space between us.

hunks.baseline: When Michael Silbert twisted aside and dodged the spears, I tore through the darkness surrounding us again and closed in right in front of him.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert twisted aside to dodge them. I tore through the darkness around us again and closed in on him.

hunks.baseline: Beyond his furious shout came the heavy whistle of a weapon cutting through the air.
hunks.sol: His furious shout was swallowed by the heavy rush of his sword through the air.

hunks.baseline: Supplied with an absurd amount of magical power, the now-enormous sword swung down with the force to cleave me in two.
hunks.sol: Fed an absurd amount of magical power, the enormous blade came down as if to cleave me in two.

hunks.baseline: Space split open, and the sword, having missed its target, cleaved the ground.
hunks.sol: It split the air, missed me, and cleaved the ground.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, a dull pain spread from my chest. I’d dodged to the side at the last moment, but the pressure carried by the sword was far greater and sharper than I’d imagined.
hunks.sol: Pain stung across my chest. I’d dodged sideways at the last moment, but the pressure behind the sword was stronger—and sharper—than I’d imagined.

hunks.baseline: A strength and speed that made my hair stand on end.
hunks.sol: His strength and speed made my hair stand on end.

hunks.baseline: But just as he possessed an immense amount of power I could never have, I possessed something he did not.
hunks.sol: But just as he had a vast store of power I could never possess, I had something he lacked.

hunks.baseline: In a fight where life and death hung in the balance, what mattered more than the size of one’s internal energy—
hunks.sol: Something more important than the amount of internal energy you held when your life was on the line.

hunks.baseline: Was martial arts.
hunks.sol: Martial arts.

hunks.baseline: Just as he raised his sword again, I drew up my internal energy and stamped down.
hunks.sol: As he raised his sword again, I drew up my internal energy and stamped down.

hunks.baseline: I used the Thousand-Catty Drop to bear down on his sword with tremendous weight. Michael Silbert’s eyes widened.
hunks.sol: Using the Thousand-Catty Drop, I pressed the blade beneath a crushing weight. Michael Silbert’s eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: It was only natural, if this was his first encounter with martial arts. Even I’d been astonished day after day when I first learned true martial arts from Jeok Cheongang.
hunks.sol: A natural reaction from someone encountering martial arts for the first time. I’d been astonished every day when I first learned proper martial arts from Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: But to me, he wasn’t a Master or a Disciple. He was a monster I had to kill.
hunks.sol: But Michael Silbert was neither my teacher nor my disciple. He was a monster I had to kill.

hunks.baseline: An enemy in the purest sense of the word, to whom I had no reason to offer a friendly explanation.
hunks.sol: An enemy, plain and simple. I owed him no friendly explanation.

hunks.baseline: It was already too late to pull away the hand gripping the sword hilt. When he hurriedly thrust out his other hand, I recited a command in my mind.
hunks.sol: It was too late for him to free the hand gripping his sword. As he thrust out his other hand, I gave a command in my mind.

hunks.baseline: What burst out wasn’t a deafening crash, but blood. Michael Silbert clenched his teeth as he saw the dagger that had pierced through his palm, magical power and all.
hunks.sol: Instead of a crash, blood burst out. Michael Silbert clenched his teeth at the sight of the dagger that had pierced his magical power and his palm.

hunks.baseline: His eyes were so wide they seemed about to pop out. Some unknowable realization was mixed with the pain in them.
hunks.sol: His eyes bulged, pain mingling with some realization I couldn’t read.

hunks.baseline: “This is……!”
hunks.sol: “This is…!”

hunks.baseline: Given Michael Silbert’s meticulous nature, he might already have vaguely guessed that I had an Inventory.
hunks.sol: Meticulous as he was, Michael Silbert might already have suspected I had an Inventory.

hunks.baseline: But I was stronger than he thought—and even better at improvising.
hunks.sol: But I was stronger than he thought, and better at improvising than that.

hunks.baseline: Even if he’d guessed, the result wouldn’t have changed much.
hunks.sol: Even if he’d guessed, it wouldn’t have changed much.

hunks.baseline: *The size of your internal energy is only one factor in deciding life or death.*
hunks.sol: *The amount of internal energy you have is only one factor in deciding who lives and who dies.*

hunks.baseline: The powerful opponents who had fallen at my hands were my witnesses, jury, and judge all at once.
hunks.sol: The powerful opponents who’d fallen at my hands could serve as witnesses, prosecutors, and judges all at once.

hunks.baseline: Some called me the greatest young prodigy and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. Others called me a lucky man who’d gained tremendous power through a sudden reawakening one day.
hunks.sol: Some called me the greatest young prodigy and the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. Others called me a lucky man who’d suddenly gained tremendous power through reawakening.

hunks.baseline: I would keep struggling with all my might until every bit of dirt filling this pit around me was gone. Until it finally became a clear pond.
hunks.sol: I’d fought with everything I had to clear the dirt from the pit around me. To turn it into a clear pond at last.

hunks.baseline: And yet…… I couldn’t hand my pond over to some leech. Not a mantis, not a toad—a leech.
hunks.sol: And I wasn’t about to hand that pond over to a leech. Not a mantis or a toad—a leech.

hunks.baseline: Especially not a leech that would fill that pond with blood instead of muddy water.
hunks.sol: Especially one that would fill it with blood instead of muddy water.

hunks.baseline: I swung my hand like a streak of light.
hunks.sol: My hand flashed.

hunks.baseline: Still clutching Michael Silbert’s hand, pierced by the dagger, I summoned another weapon from my Inventory and slashed, stabbed, twisted, and drove it into him wherever I could.
hunks.sol: Still clutching Michael Silbert’s dagger-pierced hand, I summoned another weapon from my Inventory. I slashed and stabbed wherever I could, twisting the weapon and driving it in deeper.

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed from his wide-open mouth. At the same time, the hand that had belatedly let go of the sword hilt drove into my side like a battering ram.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed from his wide-open mouth. At the same time, the hand that had finally let go of his sword drove toward my side like a battering ram.

hunks.baseline: The air whistled with a weight that made my skin crawl.
hunks.sol: The weight behind it made my skin crawl.

hunks.baseline: My opponent was a monster with magical power equivalent to two or three S-rank monsters combined, and enough strength to tear apart a large monster with his bare hands.
hunks.sol: He had the magical power of two or three S-rank monsters combined and enough raw strength to tear a large monster apart with his bare hands.

hunks.baseline: Even with the System having given me a body like steel, I wouldn’t come out of it unscathed if I let that attack land.
hunks.sol: The System had given me a body like steel, but I wouldn’t come away unscathed if that blow landed.

hunks.baseline: At least, if I did nothing.
hunks.sol: Not as I was.

hunks.baseline: The tremendous impact jolted my upper body. The sound of bones shifting rang out, and a little blood welled into my mouth.
hunks.sol: The impact jolted my upper body. I heard bones shift, and a little blood welled into my mouth.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert’s punch, thrown with all his might, had neither split my skin nor broken my bones.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert’s desperate punch had neither split my skin nor broken my bones.

hunks.baseline: It had only damaged part of the red-tinged armor that had suddenly appeared and wrapped around my upper body.
hunks.sol: It had only damaged part of the red-tinged armor that had appeared around my upper body.

hunks.sol: As the alert sounded in my ears, I smiled brightly at Michael Silbert, who had frozen in a daze.

hunks.sol: And in that instant—

hunks.sol: A heavy crash and tremor swept in all directions. The ground around us sank into a vast crater. At its bottom, Michael Silbert lay sprawled, coughing up blood after my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist struck him squarely in the chest.

hunks.baseline: “Khk, k-kergh……!”
hunks.sol: “Khk, k-kergh…!”

hunks.sol: The blood he coughed up pooled in the crater.

hunks.sol: His armor had long since been smashed to pieces. Blood and soot had stained his once-pale skin dark red.

hunks.baseline: “……You fucking idiot.”
hunks.sol: “…You fucking idiot.”

hunks.sol: I smiled bitterly. When I reached out, White Flame’s shaft shot into my grasp.
